question: The Commission has failed to answer the specific questions raised in parliamentary question E003508/20231. The Commission is therefore asked to answer directly each of the following questions separately: 1.

How much money has the Palestinian Authority directly and through third parties provided to the Palestinian Martyrs Fund2in the past 10 years? If the Commission does not know the exact figure, it is asked to provide an estimate.

How much money has the EU directly and through third parties contributed to the funding of the Palestinian Authority in the past 10 years? If the Commission does not know the exact figure, it is asked to provide an estimate.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.5.2024) The EU does not provide any financial assistance to Palestinian detainees and their families, ex-detainees and families of perpetrators of terrorist attacks, nor has ever contributed to the ‘allowance scheme’ referred to in the first written sub-question.

The EU has thorough ex-ante and ex-post controls and screening systems to ensure that EU funding reaches non disputable beneficiaries. In this context, detainees have always been ineligible. Between 2014 and 2020, the EU contracted an amount of around EUR 1.571 billion in relation to Palestine1.

The amount allocated for direct financial support to the Palestinian Authority through the Mécanisme Palestino-européen de Gestion de l’Aide Socio-économique (PEGASE) was around 50% of the total. Between 2021 and 2024, EUR 1.2 billion have been foreseen under the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument – Global Europe. In 2021, the amount allocated was EUR 316.

5 million, out of which PEGASE obtained 45%. In 2022, EUR 283 million was allocated, out of which PEGASE obtained 40%. In 2023, EUR 210.4 million were allocated to Palestine, out of which PEGASE obtained 56%.

EU Funding supports the financing of the most essential services to the Palestinians, contributes to the Palestinian Authority’s recurrent expenditures (health sector, social assistance for vulnerable families, salaries of civil servants), development projects on democratic governance, rule of law, water and energy and economic development, and financial assistance for the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees.
1 This designation shall not be construed as recognition of a State of Palestine and is without prejudice to the
individual positions of the Member States on this issue.
